result.analysis_summary: The video analysis reveals no visually distinguishable rowing mechanics between Work 2 (420-660s) and Work 4 (1260-1500s) despite telemetry differences in output.

findings.counterevidence: Telemetry shows Work 4 has higher watts and stroke rate, but video shows identical mechanics.
findings.direct_observation: Rower maintains consistent stroke pattern with identical body angle, handle grip, and leg drive.
findings.limitations: Video cannot resolve subtle mechanical differences that may correlate with telemetry output.
findings.title: Opening Phase Mechanics

findings.counterevidence: Telemetry indicates Work 4 is stronger, yet video shows no change in stroke sequencing.
findings.direct_observation: Hands-away timing and forward reach are visually consistent across both intervals.
findings.limitations: Visual analysis cannot detect internal force generation differences.
findings.title: Middle Phase Mechanics

findings.counterevidence: Telemetry shows Work 4 has higher output, but video shows steady rhythm in both.
findings.direct_observation: Stroke-to-stroke rhythm and posture remain unchanged in both intervals.
findings.limitations: Video cannot capture physiological or intent-based differences.
findings.title: Finish Phase Mechanics
